Name: regularization_backfire_cifar_fast
Title: When Regularization Backfires: A Quick CIFAR-10 Smoke Study with a Small CNN
Short Hypothesis: On a fixed small CIFAR-10 subset with a fixed ResNet-18 trained from scratch under a tiny fixed budget, some standard regularizers (dropout, weight decay) reduce top-1 test accuracy below an unregularized baseline.
Related Work: Regularization is applied reflexively in low-data deep learning to curb overfitting, but individual regularizers can interact badly with small-sample regimes and underperform a plain baseline. This is a deliberately tiny, fast, fully specified smoke version to verify the pipeline end to end.
Abstract: DATA LOADING: load CIFAR-10 with torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(root=os.environ.get('CIFAR_DIR','./data'), train=..., download=True); the dataset is already cached, internet is available. GPU (REQUIRED): set device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu' and move the model AND every input/target batch to device with .to(device); training on CPU is far too slow, you MUST use the GPU. DATALOADER (REQUIRED): construct every torch.utils.data.DataLoader with num_workers=0 -- multi-worker DataLoaders deadlock in this environment (WSL), so num_workers must be 0. KEEP IT SMALL AND FAST: train only 3 epochs, ONE seed (seed 0 only), batch size 128. ||| We test whether common regularizers hurt in a low-data regime under a tiny fixed budget. Use CIFAR-10 with a FIXED 5,000-image training subset (500 per class, seed 0) and the full 10,000-image test set, and a ResNet-18 from scratch (pretrained=False). Compare THREE arms only: (1) no-regularization baseline, (2) dropout p=0.3, (3) weight decay 5e-4. Metric: top-1 test accuracy (single seed). Training: SGD, lr=0.1, momentum 0.9, batch size 128, 3 epochs, no early stopping, no tuning. Deliverable: a small table of test accuracy per arm and a bar chart; note which arms fall below baseline.
Experiments: Dataset: CIFAR-10 via torchvision, root=os.environ.get('CIFAR_DIR','./data'), download=True; FIXED 5,000-image train subset (500/class, seed 0); full 10,000-image test set.
Model: torchvision ResNet-18, num_classes=10, from scratch. Move model and all batches to a CUDA device.
Budget (identical per arm): SGD lr=0.1 momentum 0.9, batch 128, 3 epochs, ONE seed (0).
Arms (3 only): (1) baseline, (2) dropout p=0.3, (3) weight decay 5e-4.
Metric: top-1 test accuracy per arm (single seed).
Deliverable: table of test accuracy per arm + a bar chart; identify arms below baseline.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 3 epochs and a single seed give noisy, non-final accuracies -- this is a fast smoke run, not a publication-grade result.
Findings are specific to ResNet-18 and the 5k CIFAR-10 subset.
